description: Phase A (KFT completion). Stand up the standalone conformance validator for the KFT §3 job manifest — an ajv (TS) + jsonschema (Python) validator plus conformance CI for `finetune-job.schema.json`, run through the SAME two-validator smoke every other artifact passes (`make check-conformance`, node `schemas/src/validate.ts` + `agora_provider_router.artifact_validator`). This is structural admission ONLY: the semantic gate (modality×method, egress, spend) stays in the providers (trainer/README.md §'Admission' + the specialized providers), NOT here. The three vendored copies of the schema (`schemas/src/koine-schemas/finetune-job.schema.json`, `trainer/src/agora_trainer/schemas/finetune-job.schema.json`, and the `schemas/src/conformance/fixtures/finetune-job.json` fixture) must stay byte-identical to koine and be drift-gated. agora gates on `make check`; the touched areas gate on `make check-schemas` / `make check-conformance` / `make check-trainer`.

userStories.title: finetune-job joins the two-validator conformance artifact set
userStories.description: Add `finetune-job` to the `ARTIFACTS` set so both validator CLIs — node `schemas/src/validate.ts` (ajv) and `agora_provider_router.artifact_validator` (Python jsonschema) — smoke it, and add the golden pass fixture the smoke replays. The validator is purely structural against KFT §3; it makes no modality/egress/spend judgement.
acceptanceCriteria: `finetune-job` is added to the Makefile `ARTIFACTS` set (or the equivalent list `check-conformance` loops), so `make check-conformance` validates it through BOTH the ajv (TS) and jsonschema (Python) CLIs against a golden fixture, and a KFT §3-conformant `finetune-job.json` fixture passes both with exit 0.

The validator emits agora's standard exit-code semantics — 0 ok / 1 invalid / 2 usage — on both CLIs for a well-formed and a malformed job; a hand-mutated invalid job (e.g. missing a §3 required field) is rejected 1 by both.
No semantic admission is added here (no modality×method, egress, or spend logic — that stays in the providers per trainer/README.md); `make check` green.

userStories.title: Byte-identical schema pin across the three vendored copies
userStories.description: The finetune-job schema is vendored in three places (schemas koine-schemas, the trainer's package copy, and the conformance fixture set) and each must stay byte-for-byte with koine's source of truth. Add a drift gate so a divergent copy fails, matching the repo's cross-language-pin discipline (progress.txt 'Cross-language pins make file paths API').
acceptanceCriteria: A drift test asserts `schemas/src/koine-schemas/finetune-job.schema.json` and `trainer/src/agora_trainer/schemas/finetune-job.schema.json` are byte-identical to each other (and to koine's `specs/` copy where reachable), failing loudly on any divergence — the schema is pinned, never forked.
The test runs under the existing gates (vitest via `make check-schemas`, pytest via `make check-trainer`), not a new one-off runner; `make check-schemas` and `make check-trainer` green.

userStories.title: Wire the validator into CI and document the scope boundary
userStories.description: Make the finetune-job conformance step part of `make check` (what CI runs) and document that this tasklist delivers structural validation only — the KFT semantic admission (modality×method per FT-F, the §4.2 egress gate, the §7 spend ceiling) lives in the trainer and specialized providers, never in the shared validator.
acceptanceCriteria: The finetune-job validation runs as part of `make check` (via `check-conformance`), so a regression in the schema or either validator turns the gate red — the self-gating 'first gate' property the conformance step already provides.

A short doc (or a section in an existing doc / trainer/README.md follow-up) records that agora:41 is structural-only and names where semantic admission lives, closing the 'named-but-unbuilt agora tasklist' row in trainer/README.md.
